title: DRerio LogAI: an open-source, GPU-free platform for automated tracking and behavioural analysis of adult zebrafish (Danio rerio)

creators.name: Sant'Ana Camargos, Marco Antônio
creators.affiliation: São Paulo State University (UNESP), Botucatu, São Paulo, Brazil

description:
DRerio LogAI is an open-source desktop platform for automated tracking, closed-loop stimulation and behavioural analysis of adult zebrafish (Danio rerio). It combines YOLOv11 detection, BYTETracker multi-object tracking and Intel OpenVINO inference in an event-driven architecture, and runs GPU-free on integrated graphics.

Any weight, any class (release 8). The platform was built around zebrafish, and up to release 7 it assumed a weight with exactly two classes (the tank and the fish) and an analysis that starts on the first frame where the fish is seen. Release 8 removes both assumptions. Any YOLOv8/YOLOv11 detection weight can be used once each of its classes is given a role: subject (the animal that is tracked and measured), arena (the apparatus: tank, open field, maze), context (objects that are recorded frame by frame but never tracked, such as the experimenter's hand or a start box) or ignored. Roles are set for a weight, for a project or in the project wizard, and are stored by class name, so a retrained weight with an extra class does not shift them. A weight with three or more named classes and no recognisable subject is refused instead of tracking whatever class happens to come first. Each recording can also have its own start and end of analysis, defined by conditions on those classes, on entries into regions of interest, on time, on an Arduino signal or on a manual mark, and evaluated on the recording's own clock (video timestamps for pre-recorded files, capture instants for live sessions). The video is always recorded in full and only the metrics are restricted to the window. The motivating case is the Barnes maze: a top-down rat video recorded at about 9.9 frames per second with a variable frame interval, where the rat must only be measured after the experimenter leaves and the start box is lifted, and the trial ends when the rat enters the escape hole. Behavioural defaults are no longer fixed to zebrafish: geotaxis is disabled in top-down views, and the thigmotaxis band and the plausible-speed ceiling are set per project, with a built-in rodent top-view template. The trained weights distributed with the software are the zebrafish weights; a weight for another species is supplied by the user, who declares the role of each of its classes.

This archive. Snapshot of the source code at tag v8.0.0, deposited as the citable code object for the associated manuscripts. The validation and benchmark results reported in those manuscripts were produced with release 4.0.0, which remains available as tag v4.0.0 for exact reproduction; releases 5, 6 and 7 optimised the detector plugins, the user interface and internationalisation, and refined the closed-loop session logger; release 8 accepts any YOLO detection weight through per-class roles (subject, arena, context, ignored) and adds start/stop analysis windows evaluated on the recording's own clock. The analysis scripts and the paired coordinate tables that regenerate every reported statistic are deposited separately (see related identifiers).

Licensing. The original source code of this repository is licensed MIT, copyright Universidade Estadual Paulista (UNESP). The application as distributed is effectively licensed AGPL-3.0-or-later, because it packages and requires Ultralytics YOLO (AGPL-3.0). The trained YOLOv11 weights are not part of this source archive: they are published as assets of a separate GitHub release and installed by the bundled fetch-weights command, which verifies each file against a SHA-256 recorded in weights_manifest.json. Those weights are Ultralytics derivatives and are likewise effectively AGPL-3.0; their training imagery derives from the ZebraFish-Detection dataset (Roboflow Universe), licensed CC BY 4.0, which requires attribution.
